claim: The claustrum complex is viewed as fundamental for higher-order cognition.
source: The claustrum complex is viewed as fundamental for higher-order cognition; however, the circuit organization and function of its neuroanatomical subregions are not well understood.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that references established views in the field.

claim: The circuit organization and function of the claustrum complex's neuroanatomical subregions are not well understood.
source: The claustrum complex is viewed as fundamental for higher-order cognition; however, the circuit organization and function of its neuroanatomical subregions are not well understood.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: A subpopulation of EN neurons was identified by their projection to the ventral CA1 (ENvCA1-proj. neurons).
source: We identified a subpopulation of EN neurons by their projection to the ventral CA1 (ENvCA1-proj. neurons), embedded in recurrent circuits with other EN neurons and the piriform cortex.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's experimental work.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. neurons are embedded in recurrent circuits with other EN neurons and the piriform cortex.
source: We identified a subpopulation of EN neurons by their projection to the ventral CA1 (ENvCA1-proj. neurons), embedded in recurrent circuits with other EN neurons and the piriform cortex.
evidence: This is supported by the monosynaptic rabies tracing data presented in Figure 6.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. neuron activity was biased toward novelty across stimulus categories.
source: Although the ENvCA1-proj. neuron activity was biased toward novelty across stimulus categories, their chemogenetic inhibition selectively disrupted the memory-guided but not innate responses of mice to novelty.
evidence: This is supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Chemogenetic inhibition of ENvCA1-proj. neurons selectively disrupted the memory-guided but not innate responses of mice to novelty.
source: Although the ENvCA1-proj. neuron activity was biased toward novelty across stimulus categories, their chemogenetic inhibition selectively disrupted the memory-guided but not innate responses of mice to novelty.
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic inhibition experiments shown in Figure 8.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. neurons serve as an essential node for recognition memory through recurrent circuits mediating sustained attention to novelty.
source: Based on our functional connectivity analysis, we suggest that ENvCA1-proj. neurons serve as an essential node for recognition memory through recurrent circuits mediating sustained attention to novelty, and through feed-forward inhibition of distal vCA1 neurons shifting memory-guided behavior from familiarity to novelty.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the combined data from connectivity and functional studies.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. neurons serve as an essential node for recognition memory through feed-forward inhibition of distal vCA1 neurons shifting memory-guided behavior from familiarity to novelty.
source: Based on our functional connectivity analysis, we suggest that ENvCA1-proj. neurons serve as an essential node for recognition memory through recurrent circuits mediating sustained attention to novelty, and through feed-forward inhibition of distal vCA1 neurons shifting memory-guided behavior from familiarity to novelty.
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiology data showing feedforward inhibition in Figure 5.

claim: The claustrum complex is an evolutionarily conserved brain region found across mammalian species, reptiles, and birds.
source: The claustrum (CLA) complex, an evolutionarily conserved brain region found across mammalian species, reptiles, and birds, is hypothesized to serve as a node for establishing higher-order cognitive functions by coordinating neuronal activity on a global scale (Narikiyo et al., 2020; Norimoto et al., 2020; Crick and Koch, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The claustrum complex is hypothesized to serve as a node for establishing higher-order cognitive functions by coordinating neuronal activity on a global scale.
source: The claustrum (CLA) complex, an evolutionarily conserved brain region found across mammalian species, reptiles, and birds, is hypothesized to serve as a node for establishing higher-order cognitive functions by coordinating neuronal activity on a global scale (Narikiyo et al., 2020; Norimoto et al., 2020; Crick and Koch, 2005).
evidence: This hypothesis is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The claustrum complex has extensive connections with many cortical and subcortical areas.
source: This view is based on its extensive connections with many cortical and subcortical areas (Smith et al., 2020; Goll et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous anatomical studies.

claim: Functions of the claustrum complex include sensory perception and attention, which may affect memory processing, including working memory, associative memory, and recognition memory.
source: Some of these functions include sensory perception and attention, which may affect memory processing, including working memory, associative memory, and recognition memory (Gardiner and Parkin, 1990; Siegel and Castel, 2018; Oberauer, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on memory and cognition.

claim: Abnormalities of the CLA complex are found in major cognitive disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorders.
source: Consistent with this view, abnormalities of the CLA complex is found in major cognitive disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorders (Chen et al., 2023; Cascella et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Microcircuitry and functional segregation of the individual constituents of the CLA complex have remained unclear.
source: However, microcircuitry and functional segregation of the individual constituents of the CLA complex have remained unclear.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The cytoarchitecture and genetic expression broadly divide the CLA complex into dorsal and ventral parts.
source: The cytoarchitecture and genetic expression broadly divide the CLA complex into dorsal and ventral parts, with the dorsal part typically referred to as 'CLA' and the ventral part having its own nomenclature: 'EN' in rodents (Smith et al., 2019; Grimstvedt et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous anatomical studies.

claim: The dorsal part of the CLA complex is typically referred to as 'CLA' and the ventral part is referred to as 'EN' in rodents.
source: The cytoarchitecture and genetic expression broadly divide the CLA complex into dorsal and ventral parts, with the dorsal part typically referred to as 'CLA' and the ventral part having its own nomenclature: 'EN' in rodents (Smith et al., 2019; Grimstvedt et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous anatomical studies.

claim: The CLA forms reciprocal connections with dorsal cortices containing sensory, motor, and association areas generating diverse physiological effects depending on the cortical targets and their activity patterns.
source: Current evidence indicates that the CLA forms reciprocal connections with dorsal cortices containing sensory, motor, and association areas generating diverse physiological effects depending on the cortical targets and their activity patterns (Smith et al., 2020; Goll et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: EN primarily provides inputs to the piriform cortex and limbic systems.
source: In contrast, EN primarily provides inputs to the piriform cortex and limbic systems (Behan and Haberly, 1999; Majak and Moryś, 2007), suggesting its distinct circuit organization and role in bridging olfactory information processed by the piriform cortex and memory processed by the limbic systems (Fu et al., 2004; Watson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous anatomical studies.

claim: EN has a distinct circuit organization and role in bridging olfactory information processed by the piriform cortex and memory processed by the limbic systems.
source: In contrast, EN primarily provides inputs to the piriform cortex and limbic systems (Behan and Haberly, 1999; Majak and Moryś, 2007), suggesting its distinct circuit organization and role in bridging olfactory information processed by the piriform cortex and memory processed by the limbic systems (Fu et al., 2004; Watson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The ventral CA1 (vCA1) is known to coordinate in a range of behaviors related to exploration and recognition memory.
source: One of the distinct targets of EN, the ventral CA1 (vCA1), is known to coordinate in a range of behaviors related to exploration and recognition memory, and these functions are thought to be regulated by its afferent inputs in a domain-specific manner (Pi et al., 2020; Ciocchi et al., 2015; Hunsaker et al., 2008; Okuyama et al., 2016; Kesner et al., 2011; Meira et al., 2018; Tanimizu et al., 2017; Titulaer et al., 2021; Broadbent et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: vCA1 functions are thought to be regulated by its afferent inputs in a domain-specific manner.
source: One of the distinct targets of EN, the ventral CA1 (vCA1), is known to coordinate in a range of behaviors related to exploration and recognition memory, and these functions are thought to be regulated by its afferent inputs in a domain-specific manner (Pi et al., 2020; Ciocchi et al., 2015; Hunsaker et al., 2008; Okuyama et al., 2016; Kesner et al., 2011; Meira et al., 2018; Tanimizu et al., 2017; Titulaer et al., 2021; Broadbent et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: EN is a key node for the establishment of recognition memory.
source: We, therefore, hypothesized that EN is a key node for the establishment of recognition memory.
evidence: This is the hypothesis tested in the study.

claim: EN vCA1-proj. neurons innervated multiple components of the limbic system except the amygdala and prefrontal cortex.
source: We found EN vCA1-proj. neurons innervated multiple components of the limbic system except the amygdala and prefrontal cortex and produced potent feedforward inhibitory control over vCA1 pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the intersectional tracing data shown in Figure 2.

claim: EN vCA1-proj. neurons produced potent feedforward inhibitory control over vCA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: We found EN vCA1-proj. neurons innervated multiple components of the limbic system except the amygdala and prefrontal cortex and produced potent feedforward inhibitory control over vCA1 pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5.

claim: During the recognition memory test, the activity of EN vCA1-proj. neurons were condensed around conspecifics or objects where mice spent most time on.
source: During the recognition memory test, the activity of EN vCA1-proj. neurons were condensed around conspecifics or objects where mice spent most time on.
evidence: This is supported by the fiber photometry data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Disruption of EN vCA1-proj. activity only impaired memory-guided exploration of novel stimuli without affecting innate exploration induced by novelty.
source: However, disruption of EN vCA1-proj. activity only impaired memory-guided exploration of novel stimuli without affecting innate exploration induced by novelty.
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic inhibition experiments shown in Figure 8.

claim: EN subserves some of the key functions required for recognition memory governed by specific limbic systems.
source: These findings demonstrate that EN subserves some of the key functions required for recognition memory governed by specific limbic systems.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: A retrograde tracer (60 nl) was injected into the vCA1 of mice to assess the significance of EN as a vCA1 afferent.
source: To assess the significance of EN as a vCA1 afferent, we injected a retrograde tracer (60 nl) into the vCA1 of mice and compared the number of the retrogradely labeled neurons in the EN and other brain regions (Figure 1A and B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Methods).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Labeled neurons were found in multiple areas including the septum, entorhinal cortex, and basolateral amygdala.
source: We found labeled neurons in multiple areas including the septum, entorhinal cortex, and basolateral amygdala (Figure 1C–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B; Tao et al., 2021; Gergues et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by the retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 1 and citations to previous studies.

claim: Prominent labeling was observed in the area defined as EN in Allen Brain Atlas.
source: In addition to these well-known vCA1 afferents, prominent labeling was observed in the area defined as EN in Allen Brain Atlas (Figure 1G, Methods).
evidence: This is supported by the retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The number of presynaptic neurons in EN was ~10-fold lower than the entorhinal cortex.
source: The number of presynaptic neurons in EN was ~10- fold lower than the entorhinal cortex (data not shown).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison from the retrograde tracing data.

claim: The normalized count of presynaptic neurons in EN was significantly greater than the basolateral amygdala, lateral septum, and medial septum.
source: However, the normalized count of presynaptic neurons in EN was significantly greater than the basolateral amygdala, lateral septum, and medial septum (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative analysis shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The vCA1-projecting neurons in the EN were spread along an antero-posterior axis with two peak densities, one in anterior and another in posterior to the bregma.
source: The vCA1-projecting neurons in the EN were spread along an antero-posterior axis with two peak densities, one in anterior and another in posterior to the bregma (Figure 1I and J).
evidence: This is supported by the spatial distribution analysis shown in Figure 1I and J.

claim: Number of labeled neurons was greater in posterior EN.
source: Number of labeled neurons was greater in posterior EN (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The same analysis along the dorso-ventral axis showed a single dominant peak at the depth consistent with the location of EN.
source: In contrast, the same analysis along the dorso-ventral axis showed a single dominant peak at the depth consistent with the location of EN (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the spatial distribution analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: A retrograde tracer (60 nl for each) was injected in one color into vCA1 and a retrograde tracer in another color into a cortical area known to receive projections from EN or 'CLA'.
source: To further confirm the location of these vCA1-projecting neurons, we injected a retrograde tracer (60 nl for each) in one color into vCA1 and a retrograde tracer in another color into a cortical area known to receive projections from EN or 'CLA' representing a dorsal part of CLA complex (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: The prefrontal cortex was targeted to label EN, and the anterior cingulate cortex, the motor cortex, and the dorsomedial entorhinal cortex were targeted to label CLA.
source: We targeted the prefrontal cortex to label EN, and the anterior cingulate cortex, the motor cortex, and the dorsomedial entorhinal cortex to label CLA (Figure 2C–F; Kitanishi and Matsuo, 2017; Qadir et al., 2018; Jackson et al., 2018; Smith and Alloway, 2010).
evidence: This describes the experimental method and is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is a major spatial overlap in labeling of vCA1-projecting neurons with prefrontal cortex-projecting neurons, but not with other cortical projection neurons.
source: We found there is a major spatial overlap in labeling of vCA1-projecting neurons with prefrontal cortex-projecting neurons, but not with other cortical projection neurons (Figure 2G–J).
evidence: This is supported by the dual retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 2G–J.

claim: Around 30% of vCA1-projecting neurons were found to be double-labeled when a cortical injection was made into the prefrontal cortex.
source: Moreover, around 30% of vCA1-projecting neurons were found to be double-labeled when a cortical injection was made into the prefrontal cortex, suggesting some vCA1-projecting neurons send axons to this cortical area (Figure 2K and L).
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2K.

claim: Some vCA1-projecting neurons send axons to the prefrontal cortex.
source: Moreover, around 30% of vCA1-projecting neurons were found to be double-labeled when a cortical injection was made into the prefrontal cortex, suggesting some vCA1-projecting neurons send axons to this cortical area (Figure 2K and L).
evidence: This is inferred from the double-labeling data shown in Figure 2K.

claim: An intersectional approach was used to label the somata and axons of vCA1-projecting EN neurons with eGFP.
source: To further determine the cortical and subcortical innervation pattern of vCA1-projecting EN neurons, we used an intersectional approach to label their somata and axons with eGFP. CAV2-Cre (60 nl) was injected into the vCA1 and flox-eGFP (100 nl) was injected into the EN (Figure 2M).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Apart from vCA1, axons from vCA1-projecting neurons were found in various cortical areas including the prefrontal cortex, lateral entorhinal cortex, and the piriform cortex.
source: Apart from vCA1, axons from vCA1-projecting neurons were found in various cortical areas including the prefrontal cortex, lateral entorhinal cortex, and the piriform cortex (Figure 2N–P and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This is supported by the intersectional tracing data shown in Figure 2N–P.

claim: Projection to the prefrontal cortex was much sparser relative to that of vCA1.
source: Projection to the prefrontal cortex was much sparser relative to that of vCA1, as expected based on the retrograde labeling data (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is supported by the intersectional tracing data and is consistent with the retrograde labeling data.

claim: The connectivity of vCA1-projecting EN neurons to the amygdala was sparse relative to vCA1.
source: The connectivity of vCA1-projecting EN neurons to the amygdala, which represents the major component of limbic systems, was also sparse relative to vCA1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), indicating vCA1 is the main target of these EN neurons in this system.
evidence: This is supported by the intersectional tracing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: vCA1 is the main target of EN neurons in the limbic system.
source: The connectivity of vCA1-projecting EN neurons to the amygdala, which represents the major component of limbic systems, was also sparse relative to vCA1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), indicating vCA1 is the main target of these EN neurons in this system.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of projection densities.

claim: Within the hippocampus, very sparse EN axons were observed in vCA3 and dentate gyrus.
source: Within the hippocampus, very sparse EN axons were observed in vCA3 and dentate gyrus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the intersectional tracing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: EN represents a major afferent of vCA1.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate EN represents a major afferent of vCA1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the retrograde tracing data.

claim: EN neurons projecting their axons to vCA1 also send strong collaterals to the lateral entorhinal cortex and piriform cortex, but relatively weak to the prefrontal cortex or other limbic structures.
source: Moreover, EN neurons projecting their axons to vCA1 also send strong collaterals to the lateral entorhinal cortex and piriform cortex, but relatively weak to the prefrontal cortex or other limbic structures.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the intersectional tracing data.

claim: An anterograde tracer (AAV-GFP, 60 nl) was injected into the EN to investigate the projection pattern of EN axons in the hippocampus.
source: We next investigated the projection pattern of EN axons in the hippocampus by injecting an anterograde tracer (AAV-GFP, 60 nl) into the EN (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: EN axons were mostly confined in the SLM layer of the distal part of vCA1.
source: Analysis of different parts of the hippocampal section indicated EN axons were mostly confined in the SLM layer of the distal part of vCA1 (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is supported by the anterograde tracing data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Projection to intermediate or dorsal CA1 was limited or undetectable.
source: Projection to intermediate or dorsal CA1 was limited or undetectable (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This is supported by the anterograde tracing data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: SLM mainly consists of GABAergic neurons.
source: Since SLM mainly consists of GABAergic neurons (Pelkey et al., 2017), we hypothesized that EN axons form synapses with this cell type.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: EN axons form synapses with GABAergic neurons in SLM.
source: Since SLM mainly consists of GABAergic neurons (Pelkey et al., 2017), we hypothesized that EN axons form synapses with this cell type.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that was tested using monosynaptic rabies tracing.

claim: The monosynaptic rabies tracing technique was applied to Vgat-Cre mice to test if EN axons form synapses with GABAergic neurons.
source: To test this, we first applied the monosynaptic rabies tracing technique to Vgat-Cre mice (Figure 4A, Methods).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: The distribution of starter cells was confirmed to be within the ventral-intermediate region of the hippocampus using AMaSiNe.
source: The distribution of starter cells (identified by GFP and mCherry co-labeling) was confirmed to be within the ventral-intermediate region of the hippocampus using AMaSiNe (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1; Song et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by the spatial mapping data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Presynaptic neurons were consistently observed in EN in addition to other expected areas (e.g. septum and entorhinal cortex).
source: In these mice, the presynaptic neurons were consistently observed in EN in addition to other expected areas (e.g. septum and entorhinal cortex) (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-F; Freund and Antal, 1988; Bilash et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by the monosynaptic rabies tracing data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The density of the presynaptic neurons in EN was greater at the posterior region to the bregma.
source: The density of the presynaptic neurons in EN was greater at the posterior region to the bregma (Figure 4D), consistent with our earlier observation (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: EN axons preferentially innervate the GABAergic neurons spanning across the Py-SR border to the SR-SLM border in distal vCA1.
source: Taken together, these results indicate EN axons preferentially innervate the GABAergic neurons spanning across the Py-SR border to the SR-SLM border in distal vCA1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the optogenetic mapping data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Connection probability and strength of EN axons were lowest in neurons in SLM compared to neurons in other layers.
source: However, contrary to the expectation, connection probability and strength were lowest in neurons in SLM compared to neurons in other layers (Figure 4H–J).
evidence: This is supported by the optogenetic mapping data shown in Figure 4H–J.

claim: SLM contains the apical tuft dendrite of pyramidal neurons, which could be a target of EN axons in addition to GABAergic neurons.
source: SLM also contains the apical tuft dendrite of pyramidal neurons, which could be a target of EN axons in addition to GABAergic neurons.
evidence: This is based on known anatomy of the hippocampus.

claim: ChR2 was expressed in EN axons and whole-cell recording was made from pyramidal neurons in distal vCA1 in the presence of TTX and 4-AP to test if pyramidal neurons are targets of EN axons.
source: To test this, we expressed ChR2 in EN axons but made whole-cell recording from pyramidal neurons in distal vCA1 in the presence of TTX and 4-AP.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: CA1 pyramidal neurons can be differentiated into superficial and deep-layer neurons with distinct anatomy and function.
source: Since CA1 pyramidal neurons can be differentiated into superficial and deep-layer neurons with distinct anatomy and function (Danielson et al., 2016), we recorded from neurons in each layer as well as nearby GABAergic neurons at the Py-SR and SR-SLM borders for the comparison (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Monosynaptic input to superficial and deep layer pyramidal neurons was similar.
source: We found monosynaptic input to superficial and deep layer pyramidal neurons was similar, and monosynaptic input to pyramidal neurons (superficial and deep pooled) and GABAergic neurons was also comparable (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Monosynaptic input to pyramidal neurons (superficial and deep pooled) and GABAergic neurons was comparable.
source: We found monosynaptic input to superficial and deep layer pyramidal neurons was similar, and monosynaptic input to pyramidal neurons (superficial and deep pooled) and GABAergic neurons was also comparable (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: EN axons innervated multiple GABAergic neurons across different layers.
source: Since EN axons innervated multiple GABAergic neurons across different layers, we hypothesized they may exert stronger inhibition onto pyramidal neurons through feed-forward inhibition.
evidence: This is based on the connectivity data shown in Figure 4.

claim: EN axons may exert stronger inhibition onto pyramidal neurons through feed-forward inhibition.
source: Since EN axons innervated multiple GABAergic neurons across different layers, we hypothesized they may exert stronger inhibition onto pyramidal neurons through feed-forward inhibition.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that was tested using electrophysiology.

claim: Photo-stimulation of EN axons evoked EPSCs in the majority of pyramidal neurons in both superficial and deep layers.
source: At the command potential of –70 mV, photo-stimulation of EN axons evoked EPSCs in the majority of pyramidal neurons in both layers (7 out of 10 neurons in superficial and 5 out of 10 neurons in deep) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: At the command potential of +12 mV, photo-stimulation of EN axons evoked outward postsynaptic current in pyramidal neurons, including those without EPSCs.
source: At the command potential of +12 mV, the same stimulation evoked outward postsynaptic current in the same neurons, including those without EPSCs (10 out of 10 for superficial and deep) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The outward current evoked by EN axon stimulation was abolished by the application of TTX and 4-AP or gabazine.
source: This outward current was abolished by the application of TTX and 4-AP or gabazine (10 µM), indicating it is disynaptically driven and mediated by the inhibitory GABAA receptor (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The outward current evoked by EN axon stimulation is disynaptically driven and mediated by the inhibitory GABAA receptor.
source: This outward current was abolished by the application of TTX and 4-AP or gabazine (10 µM), indicating it is disynaptically driven and mediated by the inhibitory GABAA receptor (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is inferred from the pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The strength of IPSCs overwhelmed the EPSCs in all pyramidal neurons tested.
source: When the relative strength of EPSCs and IPSCs were compared for each neuron, the strength of IPSCs overwhelmed the EPSCs in all cases (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: EN axons disynaptically inhibit pyramidal neurons in vCA1.
source: This indicates EN axons disynaptically inhibit pyramidal neurons in vCA1 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiology data.

claim: Retrograde CAV2-Cre was injected into vCA1 to express Cre into ENvCA1-proj. neurons, then the monosynaptic rabies tracing technique was applied to specifically label its presynaptic neurons in wild-type mice.
source: To address this, retrograde CAV2-Cre was injected into vCA1 to express Cre into ENvCA1-proj. neurons, then applied the monosynaptic rabies tracing technique to specifically label its presynaptic neurons in wild-type mice (Figure 6A).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: The piriform cortex contained the highest number of presynaptic neurons followed by EN.
source: We found the piriform cortex contained the highest number of presynaptic neurons followed by EN (Figure 6D–F).
evidence: This is supported by the monosynaptic rabies tracing data shown in Figure 6D–F.

claim: Within the piriform cortex, layer 2 neurons were the major source of afferent to ENvCA1-proj. neurons.
source: Within the piriform cortex, layer 2 neurons were the major source of afferent (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6G.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. neurons receive major input from piriform cortex and form a recurrent connection with neurons in EN.
source: These data indicate ENvCA1-proj. neurons receive major input from piriform cortex and form a recurrent connection with neurons in EN (Figure 6H).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the monosynaptic rabies tracing data.

claim: GCaMP8s was expressed in ENvCA1-proj. neurons and their activity was monitored using fiber photometry while video recording mice performing a social recognition memory test.
source: To determine whether and how the activity of EN neurons is related to this function, we expressed GCaMP8s in ENvCA1-proj. neurons and monitored their activity using fiber photometry while video recording mice performing a social recognition memory tests consisting of a pretest, sociability test, and discrimination test (Figure 7A and B, Methods).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: The nose position of the subject mouse was tracked during tests using DeepLabCut.
source: The nose position of the subject mouse was tracked during tests using DeepLabCut (Figure 7C; Mathis et al., 2018; Lauer et al., 2022), and cumulative time and calcium events were mapped onto the arena space (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used and is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cumulative time and calcium events were correlated in space across all sessions.
source: We found these values were correlated in space across all sessions (i.e. the more time the mice spent in a given space, the more the ENvCA1-proj. activity), including in the open field with no object or in the test arena with conspecifics or objects (Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A-B).
evidence: This is supported by the fiber photometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: The more time the mice spent in a given space, the more the ENvCA1-proj. activity.
source: We found these values were correlated in space across all sessions (i.e. the more time the mice spent in a given space, the more the ENvCA1-proj. activity), including in the open field with no object or in the test arena with conspecifics or objects (Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A-B).
evidence: This is supported by the fiber photometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Cumulative calcium events of ENvCA1-proj. neurons became high towards the space around objects or conspecifics when they were present.
source: Cumulative calcium events of ENvCA1-proj. neurons became high towards the space around objects or conspecifics when they were present and were correlated with interaction times except for sociability session (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C-D).
evidence: This is supported by the fiber photometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2C-D.

claim: Cumulative calcium events were correlated with interaction times except for sociability session.
source: Cumulative calcium events of ENvCA1-proj. neurons became high towards the space around objects or conspecifics when they were present and were correlated with interaction times except for sociability session (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C-D).
evidence: This is supported by the fiber photometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2C-D.

claim: In the sociability session, the cumulative calcium events around a novel conspecific and object were similar despite mice spending more time on conspecifics.
source: In the sociability session, the cumulative calcium events around a novel conspecific and object were similar despite mice spending more time on conspecifics (Figure 7E left, Figure 7—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by the fiber photometry data shown in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 2C.

claim: In the social discrimination test, both the cumulative time and cumulative ENvCA1-proj. activity was higher for an unfamiliar than familiar conspecific.
source: In contrast, in the social discrimination test, both the cumulative time and cumulative ENvCA1-proj. activity was higher for an unfamiliar than familiar conspecific (Figure 7D–E, Figure 7—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by the fiber photometry data shown in Figure 7D–E and Figure 7—figure supplement 2C.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. activity and behavior had a greater degree of correlation in social discrimination than sociability.
source: As a result, ENvCA1-proj. activity and behavior had a greater degree of correlation in social discrimination than sociability.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of correlations across different sessions.

claim: A similar correlation between ENvCA1-proj. activity and behavior occurs in a non-social context (object discrimination test).
source: We also tested if a similar correlation occurs in a non-social context by recording ENvCA1-proj. activity and behavior in the object discrimination test (Figure 7F). The cumulative time and calcium events were significantly correlated across different sessions i.e., familiarization, and object discrimination (Figure 7G, Figure 7—figure supplement 2E), largely consistent with the findings in the social discrimination test.
evidence: This is supported by the fiber photometry data shown in Figure 7G and Figure 7—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The activity of ENvCA1-proj. neurons are generally correlated with the time the mouse spends in a particular location at the basal level (i.e. open field) or task conditions.
source: These data indicate that the activity of ENvCA1-proj. neurons are generally correlated with the time the mouse spends in a particular location at the basal level (i.e. open field) or task conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the fiber photometry data.

claim: The degree of correlation between ENvCA1-proj. activity and behavior appears to vary depending on the session, such that it was highest in the pretest/familiarization and social/object discrimination test, but lowest in the sociability test.
source: However, the degree of correlation appears to vary depending on the session, such that it was highest in the pretest/familiarization and social/object discrimination test, but lowest in the sociability test.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the fiber photometry data.

claim: The activity of ENvCA1-proj. neurons was inhibited using inhibitory DREADD (hM4Di) during social and object discrimination tests.
source: To address this, we inhibited the activity of ENvCA1-proj. neurons using inhibitory DREADD (hM4Di) during social and object discrimination tests (Figure 8A–C and H, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A; Roth, 2016).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: CAV-2-Cre (60 nl) and AAV-flox-hM4Di (100 nl for each coordinate) were bilaterally injected into vCA1 and EN, respectively, to specifically express hM4Di in ENvCA1-proj. neurons.
source: To specifically express hM4Di in ENvCA1-proj. neurons, CAV-2-Cre (60 nl) and AAV-flox-hM4Di (100 nl for each coordinate) were bilaterally injected into vCA1 and EN, respectively (Figure 8A–B).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: hM4Di was replaced with tdTomato for the control group.
source: hM4Di was replaced with tdTomato for the control group.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: A protocol was made that allows within-subject comparison, such that a mouse goes through a test with clozapine-N-oxide (CNO, 1 mg/ kg) treatment and then the same test with saline treatment the next day, or vice versa.
source: We made a protocol that allows within-subject comparison, such that a mouse goes through a test with clozapine-N-oxide (CNO, 1 mg/ kg) treatment and then the same test with saline treatment the next day, or vice versa (Figure 8C and H).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: CNO treatment did not affect the pretest or sociability in the hM4Di or the control group.
source: In the social discrimination test, CNO treatment did not affect the pretest or sociability in the hM4Di or the control group, but specifically impaired social discrimination in the hM4Di group (Figure 8D–G, Figure 8—figure supplement 1B-G).
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic inhibition data shown in Figure 8D–G.

claim: CNO treatment specifically impaired social discrimination in the hM4Di group.
source: In the social discrimination test, CNO treatment did not affect the pretest or sociability in the hM4Di or the control group, but specifically impaired social discrimination in the hM4Di group (Figure 8D–G, Figure 8—figure supplement 1B-G).
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic inhibition data shown in Figure 8D–G.

claim: A similar effect of CNO treatment was observed in novel object discrimination.
source: A similar effect was also observed in novel object discrimination (Figure 8I, Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic inhibition data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: vCA1 is implicated in anxiety and associative fear memory.
source: Apart from recognition memory, vCA1 is implicated in anxiety and associative fear memory (Jimenez et al., 2018; Jimenez et al., 2020), thus, we tested the contribution of ENvCA1-proj. neurons to these functions.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The anxiety level as determined by locomotor activity and sociability was not affected by CNO treatment in the hM4Di group.
source: The anxiety level as determined by locomotor activity (Prut and Belzung, 2003) and sociability was not affected by CNO treatment in the hM4Di group (Figure 8E, Figure 8—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic inhibition data shown in Figure 8E and Figure 8—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Fear memory as assessed by the freezing response during training (with trace fear conditioning) or recall to context or tone was not affected by CNO treatment in the hM4Di group.
source: Similarly, fear memory as assessed by the freezing response during training (with trace fear conditioning) or recall to context or tone was not affected by CNO treatment in the hM4Di group (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic inhibition data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. activity is not causally related to innate exploration behavior induced by novelty, anxiety, or fear memory.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that ENvCA1-proj. activity is not causally related to innate exploration behavior induced by novelty, anxiety, or fear memory.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the chemogenetic inhibition experiments.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. activity is necessary for mice to discriminate between familiar and unfamiliar conspecific objects.
source: However, their activity is necessary for mice to discriminate between familiar and unfamiliar conspecific objects, suggesting their major role in general recognition memory.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the chemogenetic inhibition experiments.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. neurons have a major role in general recognition memory.
source: However, their activity is necessary for mice to discriminate between familiar and unfamiliar conspecific objects, suggesting their major role in general recognition memory.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the chemogenetic inhibition experiments.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. neurons were reciprocally connected with the piriform cortex representing a major downstream target of the olfactory bulb.
source: In contrast to other parts of the CLA complex, ENvCA1-proj. neurons were reciprocally connected with the piriform cortex representing a major downstream target of the olfactory bulb (Bekkers and Suzuki, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by the monosynaptic rabies tracing data and a citation to a previous study.

claim: Social odor information is crucial for discriminating conspecifics in rodents.
source: Since social odor information is crucial for discriminating conspecifics in rodents, this circuit motif may predict the predominant role of ENvCA1-proj. neurons in social recognition memory, given that social odor, can engage multiple olfactory pathways innervating the piriform cortex (Feinberg et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Social odor can engage multiple olfactory pathways innervating the piriform cortex.
source: Since social odor information is crucial for discriminating conspecifics in rodents, this circuit motif may predict the predominant role of ENvCA1-proj. neurons in social recognition memory, given that social odor, can engage multiple olfactory pathways innervating the piriform cortex (Feinberg et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The circuit motif of ENvCA1-proj. neurons may predict their predominant role in social recognition memory.
source: Since social odor information is crucial for discriminating conspecifics in rodents, this circuit motif may predict the predominant role of ENvCA1-proj. neurons in social recognition memory, given that social odor, can engage multiple olfactory pathways innervating the piriform cortex (Feinberg et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the circuit connectivity and known functions.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. neurons contributed to broader domains of recognition memory.
source: However, we found that these neurons contributed to broader domains of recognition memory.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral experiments.

claim: The inhibition of ENvCA1-proj. activity impaired both social and non-social discrimination.
source: This is supported by the observations that the inhibition of ENvCA1-proj. activity impaired both social and non-social discrimination.
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic inhibition data shown in Figure 8.

claim: In all phases of recognition memory test, EN vCA1-proj. activity was highly correlated with the time mice spent in given locations and this correlation was biased towards novel stimuli when mice were engaged in their exploration irrespective of the stimuli being social or non-social.
source: In all phases of recognition memory test, EN vCA1-proj. activity was highly correlated with the time mice spent in given locations and this correlation was biased towards novel stimuli when mice were engaged in their exploration irrespective of the stimuli being social or non-social (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the fiber photometry data.

claim: The function of ENvCA1-proj. neurons were primarily related to the detection of and attention to novel stimuli.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the function of ENvCA1-proj. neurons were primarily related to the detection of and attention to novel stimuli.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: The recurrent connections within EN potentially support the detection of and attention to novel stimuli to help establish the recognition memory.
source: The recurrent connections within EN, which is another prominent feature of ENvCA1-proj. neurons' network, potentially supporting these processes to help establish the recognition memory (Shu et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Attentional processes mediated by ENvCA1-proj. neurons can be considered of particular relevance for memory-guided behavior.
source: Attentional processes mediated by ENvCA1-proj. neurons can be considered of particular relevance for memory-guided behavior, given that inhibition of ENvCA1-proj. activity selectively impaired conspecific/object discrimination but not innate exploratory behavior provoked by novelty as seen in pretest, sociability, and familiarization (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: The correlation of ENvCA1-proj. activity with novel object preference in the pretest suggests that these neurons 'represent' the innate preference without driving it.
source: The correlation of ENvCA1-proj. activity with novel object preference in the pretest nevertheless suggests that these neurons 'represent' the innate preference without driving it.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fiber photometry and chemogenetic inhibition data.

claim: This functional specialization, likely associated with its unique circuit connectivity to the limbic system, could differentiate EN from CLA.
source: This functional specialization, likely associated with its unique circuit connectivity to the limbic system, could differentiate EN from CLA.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the circuit connectivity and functional data.

claim: Studies on EN are generally scarce.
source: Studies on EN are generally scarce, and the available evidence of EN projections to vCA1 suggests that these projections are sparse (Behan and Haberly, 1999).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the literature.

claim: The available evidence of EN projections to vCA1 suggests that these projections are sparse.
source: Studies on EN are generally scarce, and the available evidence of EN projections to vCA1 suggests that these projections are sparse (Behan and Haberly, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Potential reasons for the perception of sparse EN projections to vCA1 include the difficulty in clearly delineating the EN from CLA complex and non-uniform distribution of ENvCA1-proj. neurons along the antero-posterior axis.
source: Potential reasons include the difficulty in clearly delineating the EN from CLA complex and non-uniform distribution of ENvCA1-proj. neurons along the antero-posterior axis.
evidence: This is a speculation about why previous studies may have underestimated EN projections.

claim: By leveraging contemporary circuit analysis tools, the EN→vCA1 circuit was demonstrated to be non-trivial.
source: By leveraging contemporary circuit analysis tools, we demonstrated that the EN→vCA1 circuit is non-trivial; ENvCA1-proj. neurons were more numerous than commonly studied vCA1 afferents, including those from the septum and amygdala.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the retrograde tracing data.

claim: ENvCA1-proj. neurons were more numerous than commonly studied vCA1 afferents, including those from the septum and amygdala.
source: By leveraging contemporary circuit analysis tools, we demonstrated that the EN→vCA1 circuit is non-trivial; ENvCA1-proj. neurons were more numerous than commonly studied vCA1 afferents, including those from the septum and amygdala.
evidence: This is supported by the retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 1.

claim: EN axons exhibited a potent disynaptic inhibition of distal vCA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Moreover, these axons exhibited a potent disynaptic inhibition of distal vCA1 pyramidal neurons, indicating their major functional implications for vCA1 activity.
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5.

claim: EN axons have major functional implications for vCA1 activity.
source: Moreover, these axons exhibited a potent disynaptic inhibition of distal vCA1 pyramidal neurons, indicating their major functional implications for vCA1 activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the electrophysiology data.

claim: Although EN axons terminated at the SLM of distal vCA1, they exhibited stronger connections to GABAergic neurons spanning from the Py-SR border to the SR-SLM border than to SLM neurons.
source: Our data indicated that although EN axons terminated at the SLM of distal vCA1, they exhibited stronger connections to GABAergic neurons spanning from the Py-SR border to the SR-SLM border than to SLM neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the optogenetic mapping data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The detection of EN inputs from GABAergic neurons at the Py-SR border was surprising, considering the distance between the soma position and the EN axons.
source: The detection of EN inputs from GABAergic neurons at the Py-SR border was surprising, considering the distance between the soma position and the EN axons.
evidence: This is a statement about the unexpected nature of the finding.

claim: There are several GABAergic cell types below SLM that extend their primary dendrites into SLM, likely explaining the observed connectivity pattern.
source: However, there are several GABAergic cell types below SLM that extend their primary dendrites into SLM (Li et al., 1992; Klausberger and Somogyi, 2008), likely explaining the observed connectivity pattern.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous anatomical studies.

claim: Among GABAergic cell types below SLM are chandelier cells found at the Py-SR border, which preferentially inhibit the axon initial segments of pyramidal neurons.
source: Among these are chandelier cells found at the Py-SR border, which preferentially inhibit the axon initial segments of pyramidal neurons, and are thus well suited to exert the powerful feedforward inhibition of vCA1 pyramidal neurons observed in our recordings (Dudok et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Chandelier cells are well suited to exert the powerful feedforward inhibition of vCA1 pyramidal neurons observed in the recordings.
source: Among these are chandelier cells found at the Py-SR border, which preferentially inhibit the axon initial segments of pyramidal neurons, and are thus well suited to exert the powerful feedforward inhibition of vCA1 pyramidal neurons observed in our recordings (Dudok et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: One potential circuit effect of EN inputs is the induction of non-linear events in vCA1 pyramidal neurons by acting in concert with other afferents (e.g. lateral entorhinal cortex targeting SLM) to generate a specific output pattern in pyramidal assemblies representing task-relevant stimuli.
source: One is the induction of non-linear events in vCA1 pyramidal neurons by acting in concert with other afferents (e.g. lateral entorhinal cortex targeting SLM) (Bilash et al., 2023) to generate a specific output pattern in pyramidal assemblies representing task-relevant stimuli.
evidence: This is a speculation supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: EN inputs may improve the signal to noise ratio of the information conveyed through the lateral entorhinal cortex, CA2 (in the case of social context), and possibly other afferents (e.g. CA3).
source: Alternatively, EN inputs may improve the signal to noise ratio of the information conveyed through the lateral entorhinal cortex, CA2 (in the case of social context), and possibly other afferents (e.g. CA3) (Chiang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Another scenario is tuning of vCA1 pyramidal neurons' response to familiar stimuli through a dynamic combination of a weak monosynaptic excitatory input and strong disynaptic inhibitory input.
source: Another scenario is tuning of vCA1 pyramidal neurons' response to familiar stimuli through a dynamic combination of a weak monosynaptic excitatory input and strong disynaptic inhibitory input.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the electrophysiology data.

claim: Such mechanism suggests that at a milliseconds scale novelty (EN) and familiarity (vCA1), recognition might occur though alternating rather than the simultaneous activity of brain microcircuits.
source: Such mechanism suggests that at a milliseconds scale novelty (EN) and familiarity (vCA1), recognition might occur though alternating rather than the simultaneous activity of brain microcircuits.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the circuit connectivity and functional data.

claim: A model is proposed for the role of ENvCA1-proj. neurons in recognition memory by balancing memory-guided attentional responses to familiarity and novelty through a combination of feedforward inhibition of vCA1 (a node for recognition of familiarity) and the recurrent circuits that contribute to sustaining attention to novelty.
source: Taken together, we propose a model for the role of ENvCA1-proj. neurons in recognition memory by balancing memory-guided attentional responses to familiarity and novelty through a combination of feedforward inhibition of vCA1 (a node for recognition of familiarity) and the recurrent circuits that contribute to sustaining attention to novelty (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the combined experimental results.

claim: The model of promoting novelty detection by suppressing familiarity responses is consistent with previous observations showing that vCA1 pyramidal neurons predominantly respond to familiar stimuli whereas novelty response can only occur through activation of vCA1 interneurons.
source: The model of promoting novelty detection by suppressing familiarity responses is consistent with previous observations showing that vCA1 pyramidal neurons predominantly respond to familiar stimuli whereas novelty response can only occur through activation of vCA1 interneurons (Tao et al., 2022; Deng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Alternating activation of EN and vCA1 could prove essential for the behavioral relevance of EN activity associated with recognition memory, without affecting innate exploratory behavior to novelty.
source: Nevertheless, alternating activation of EN and vCA1 could prove essential for the behavioral relevance of EN activity associated with recognition memory, without affecting innate exploratory behavior to novelty.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the combined experimental results.

claim: Innate exploratory behavior to novelty is primarily associated with the prefrontal cortex and amygdala, areas that are only weakly targeted by ENvCA1-proj. neurons.
source: Accordingly, the latter behavior is primarily associated with the prefrontal cortex and amygdala, areas that are only weakly targeted by ENvCA1-proj. neurons (Figure 2P, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C; Wei et al., 2023; Franklin et al., 2017; Shah and Treit, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by the intersectional tracing data and citations to previous studies.

claim: Dysfunction of ENvCA1-proj. neurons could be a key contributing factor to the deficits in CLA complex function and recognition memory found in neuropsychiatric disorders.
source: In addition to advancing our understanding of the basic organization and function of brain circuits underlying higher cognitive processes, our findings suggest dysfunction of ENvCA1-proj. neurons could be a key contributing factor to the deficits in CLA complex function and recognition memory found in neuropsychiatric disorders (Chen et al., 2023; Cascella et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Discrete EN populations can emerge as pathophysiological substrates, but also as important treatment targets for key symptoms of neuropsychiatric disorders.
source: Discrete EN populations can thus emerge as pathophysiological substrates, but also as important treatment targets for key symptoms of these disorders.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings of the study.
